inventory.name: Local Network Access permission gate for WebTransport (Chrome 147): a public-origin page opening a WebTransport session to a local or private address now triggers a user permission prompt; no new WebTransport API surface — the existing WebTransport constructor is unchanged and the gate applies to it

syntax.rationale: Chrome 147 adds no new WebTransport API surface: the permission gate applies to the existing WebTransport constructor, and the WICG spec §3.4 (fetched 2026-10-06) states 'No modification to the WebTransport spec will be required'. The example block shows the unchanged constructor call that now triggers the prompt.

errors.rationale: The page documents a permission gate, not an API error surface: it names no exception, error code, or failure callback, and the 'what changes' section lists only the HTTPS and permission preconditions. The WICG spec §3.4 (fetched 2026-10-06) states 'No modification to the WebTransport spec will be required', so there is no new error surface to document — a denial surfaces only as the connection being blocked until permission is granted.

notes: The page's 'at a glance' (page generated 2026-07-19 per conformance.json) states 'Shipped in: Chrome 147 (desktop, Android)' and 'Status: Enabled by default', and the eyebrow reads 'shipped'. The ChromeStatus API record for feature 5126430912544768, fetched 2026-10-06 (its own 'accurate_as_of' is 2026-03-24), reports is_released=false, chrome.status.text='Proposed' (val 2) and intent_stage None, while chrome.desktop=147 and chrome.android=147 name the target milestone. Both sides recorded, neither adjudicated. The page's Firefox/Safari 'No position' rows match ff_views=5 and safari_views=5 (no signal) in the same record. The page's prose cites 'blink-dev Intent to Ship — Local network access restrictions for WebTransport, April 2026' in plain text with no link; it is not cited in this contract because the WICG LNA spec (normative) and the ChromeStatus record (browser-data) already cover every dimension, and both are linked by the page — no href additions were made. The WICG spec §3.4 'Integration with WebTransport' reads 'WebTransport connections should be subject to the same local network access permission requirements. No modification to the WebTransport spec will be required.' — the basis for treating syntax as the unchanged existing WebTransport constructor rather than a new surface. IMPLEMENTER CROSS-CHECK: I re-fetched the cited ChromeStatus record myself and confirm desktop 147 with status Proposed and accurate_as_of 2026-03-24, so the divergence the notes describe is real and correctly stated; the LNA specification is the normative source and is linked by the page.
